Eduard: Hey, Janice, are you having problems with the internet applications?
Janice: Yes, I am. I guess the web server is not working.
Eduard: Don't worry, we are doing maintenance to our system right now. In the meantime, let me ask you something, do you know what an internet application is?
Janice: Well, an internet application is an internet-based interactive program, and we access these applications through a web browser. You said that today we were going to talk about internet applications programming, so I studied a little.
Eduard: I'm glad. You need to know that Internet applications programming provides us some key features that include low-level and e-commerce infrastructure, interfacing with databases, data analysis and extraction, support for searching, among others.

Janice: I see, I'm reading a lot about internet applications programming, and I learned that programmers use different programming languages and programming tools in order to develop applications.
Eduard: Exactly, sometimes we combine those languages and tools if necessary. You are doing a great job, Janice. What else did you read?
Janice: Well, something interesting is that programmers are using mostly C++ to build fundamental applications, and Java to build small applications.

Eduard: Impressive, I'm happy you are doing your internship in our company, co-workers like you matter a lot here. There is something I would like to share with you as my colleague. As you know, programmers are creating powerful tools to develop applications and websites, and at some point, people with not so much knowledge about programming will be able to use those tools effectively. I think that experienced programmers like me won't be necessary in the future.
Janice: That sounds possible. I think that internet applications, websites, plugins are already evolving very quickly. For example, online shopping or site-specific search engines. But, I also believe that experienced programmers will be busy developing other amazing things.

Action Verbs and Compound Nouns used in Software Programming.
There are different kinds of verbs and nouns. Let's take a look at some action verbs and compound nouns related to software programming.

An action verb is a verb that expresses an action that a subject can actually physically do.

For example:
Johnny usually talks about that programming language all the time!
Luisa thinks that the security software is not updated.

A noun is what we use to designate people, animals, or things. A compound noun is the combination of two or more words; these extra words we add are usually adjectives or other nouns.

For example:
We have to check if the web servers are working properly.
Some of these features are used by most e-commerce web-sites.
We have to see the results of the data analysis before we take any decision.
We access these applications through a web browser.

Simple Present and Present Continuous in Affirmative, Negative and Questions
We use the simple present to talk about an action that happens regularly, and we use the present continuous to talk about an action that is currently in process at the moment of speaking.

What is an internet application?
In computing, we call internet applications to the internet-based applications used by a client through a web browser.

Common internet applications are the online information search, the online communications, and the e-commerce business. Internet applications use different internet protocols to receive requests from clients, usually web browsers, in order to relay information. These applications regularly come with plug-ins such as Silverlight, Flash, or Java to facilitate the input data process. Internet applications are located on distant servers; that means that they don't perform any operation on the user's hardware. This is the biggest difference between an internet application and a desktop application.
